$comment: Single source for the QA custom browser (WS4): which origins the browser may load, the managed Chrome enterprise policy generated from them, recording, and the network mode. build_qa_browser_policy.py turns this plus deployment values into the managed-policy file; nothing else writes that file.
name: qa-browser

app.source: the app under test: TARGET_URL, which is the frontend stack's DistributionDomainName

api.source: the app's API: the API stack's ApiUrl origin (VITE_API_URL)

cognito.source: Amplify user-pool sign-in calls the Cognito user-pool endpoint directly (frontend/src/auth/cognito.ts: userPoolId + userPoolClientId only; no OAuth domain, no identity pool)

managedPolicy.URLAllowlist: <generated: alwaysAllowed + one scheme://host[:port] entry per origin role>

recording.enableOnlyAfter: a boolean check that no QA password appears in any recording artifact of one full viewer run (match only, never print)

network.decision: owner: VPC mode needs NAT (about $32/month) plus a proxy or firewall for domain egress control; PUBLIC relies on the managed URL allow-list

deployGate: build --for-deploy refuses unless at least one recorded (non-synthetic) fixture of a full viewer run is given and every origin it requested is on the allow-list

guardConsumer.value: the generated origins, comma-separated, normalized as scheme://host:port; qa_tool_guard reads it

assumptions: Chrome's URLBlocklist/URLAllowlist certainly govern navigations. Whether they also block fetch/XHR to an unlisted origin is not settled here; measure it on the throwaway browser. The recorded-fixture gate covers both cases: every origin the app loads must be listed.
The enterprise-policies docs list s3:GetObject/GetObjectVersion on the policy prefix as a prerequisite without naming the principal; settle which role needs it when creating the throwaway browser.
The policy file is a flat JSON object of Chrome policy keys (docs: browser-enterprise-policies.html, read 2026-11-28); up to 10 files; bucket in the browser's region.
